## Verdict: REJECT (two customer-facing pages describe behaviour the code does not have)

This pull request is not ready to merge: the new public rule-sets page tells an operator that an account identifier may be written as a bare number in the rule-set file, which the loader rejects, and sends an operator whose startup failed on a table or column mismatch to a command that does not repeat that check.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` lines 135 to 140 answer a startup failure about tables or columns that do not exist with `sqllens validate -c sqllens.toml`, but plain `validate` only loads the configuration: the existence check runs under `--check-db`. An operator who follows the page sees a clean result and learns nothing about the mismatch that blocked startup. The same command is offered at lines 123 to 128 for a refused account, where it likewise cannot reproduce the refusal. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: enumerated what validate runs with and without --check-db; correcting the sentence changes no branch or output; no tool, workflow or instruction file reads the page; it is published customer-facing documentation, so limb two does not hold and the cap lands at Important -->

- VC-145: FAIL (important) — Every account identifier is a decimal string, so `"5"` and `5` are written the same way in `binding.account_ids` while `"05"` is a different value. [docs/external/rule-sets.md:125] [behavior-inert prose cap] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: the judged prose is docs/external/rule-sets.md line 125; the loader's StrictStr and decimal pattern and the request-side coercion are enumerated and agreed, so no mechanism's coverage is in dispute and making the sentence true changes no output, branch or covered set — no tool, lint, build step or agent-instruction file reads this page, but it is published customer-facing documentation, so limb two does not hold and the cap lands at Important <!— inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: enumerated the file-side StrictStr pattern and the request-side _decimal_text coercion; searched for readers of the page and found none outside prose; the page is published —> -->

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:85 declares binding.account_ids as list[RuleSetId]; line 49 defines RuleSetId = Annotated[StrictStr, StringConstraints(pattern=_ID_PATTERN)], and line 46 sets _ID_PATTERN = ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$. StrictStr rejects a bare TOML number 5 in the file, so "5" and 5 are NOT written the same way in binding.account_ids. The pattern also rejects "05" (leading zero) at load, so it is not accepted as a different value. Only request metadata is coerced (select_rule_set via _decimal_text, lines 382-390, 423-424: int 5 -> "5"). The doc at docs/external/rule-sets.md:125 is therefore wrong about the file.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (10)

<details><summary>10 items</summary>

1. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 99 says `sqllens serve` and `sqllens validate` both print a warning for an unconfirmed set. Only `validate` prints to the console; `serve` logs the warning, so where the operator sees it depends on the logging setup. (raised by 2/4 agents)
2. `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` lines 185 and 191, `docs/internal/agent/factory.md` line 87 and `docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 209 state the runner call order without the two new runners, although a sibling line in the first file was scoped by this change. (raised by 2/4 agents)
3. The architecture tree in `AGENTS.md` gains no entry for `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` or `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py`, although it lists the safety package file by file. (raised by 2/4 agents)
4. `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` line 3 records a freshness marker seven commits behind the branch head, and the intervening commits changed the code the page describes. (raised by 2/4 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/cli.py` line 167 separates `_unconfirmed_rule_sets` from the function above it with one blank line where every other top-level definition uses two. (raised by 1/4 agents)
6. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 145 tells the operator to restart the server while the same sentence says the catalog check is retried on the next request, so no restart is needed. (raised by 1/4 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/preflight.py` lines 168 to 174 turn any non-mismatch catalog failure into a preflight error carrying only the exception's class name, and the command prints that text alone, so the driver's own reason, such as a denied read of the catalog tables, reaches no log. The request-time sibling logs that cause at warning level before refusing. (raised by 1/4 agents)
8. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 420 to 425 test the parse-refusal markers before the check for a reason a guard already logged, so a guard's own internal failure whose message happened to quote a marker would be reported to the model as a statement to rewrite. No shipped message reaches that order today. (raised by 1/4 agents)
9. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 214 to 358 keep several invariants at call sites rather than in the types: the loaded-file docstring calls the file indexed while both accessors scan or rebuild, the public `confirmed` latch is written from preflight without the lock the type carries for it, the rule-set list has no minimum length, and `RuleSetSelection` constrains neither its set name nor its user number. (raised by 1/4 agents)
10. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 470 to 472 rebuild the refusal behind its own constructor, so a future stateful subclass would be re-raised half-built, and the client-facing kind is chosen by matching text owned by other modules. (raised by 1/4 agents)

- VC-128: FAIL (important) — Passing rule_sets=True adds a database rule to qualify every column and a Tool Errors rule for "Refused by the rule set:" errors, and rule_sets=False leaves the prompt unchanged. [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py:61] [behavior-inert prose cap] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the judged prose is the rule_sets parameter docstring in src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py; the builder's two conditional branches (a resolved dialect, a caller-supplied base prompt) are enumerated and agreed, so no mechanism's coverage is in dispute and making the sentence true changes no output, branch taken or covered set — searched the repository for readers of that docstring and found only prose cross-references under docs/internal, no script, workflow or instruction file, and the docstring is never printed to a user, so all three slots hold and the cap lands at Suggestion <!— inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: enumerated the builder's dialect and base-prompt branches; no tool or agent-instruction file reads the docstring; it is never printed —> -->

The docstring at lines 61-64 states both rules are added whenever rule_sets=True, which is wrong for these inputs. The base_prompt input is a public constructor parameter. The rule_sets=False half holds (the rules are gated on self.rule_sets).

  </details>

</details>

- [ ] With the new config key naming a valid version-1 rule-set file and a MySQL `database.url`, `sqllens validate` exits 0 and `sqllens serve` starts.
- [ ] A rule-set file with an unknown field in any record, a missing required field, a wrong-typed value (a Boolean where a number is expected, a TOML date for `generated_on` and a `role_id` other than its set's `name` included), an ID with a leading zero or a non-digit, an identifier outside `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, a duplicate set or table name, a duplicate entry in any list (`columns = ["id", "name", "id"]` included), a predicate column also listed in `columns`, `metadata` key names that are not three distinct identifiers, or a `metadata` key name that SQL Lens reserves (`starter_ui_request`, `ui_features_available`) makes `sqllens validate` exit 2 and `sqllens serve` refuse to start, and the error names the record and the problem (at minimum these cases).
- [ ] A rule-set file whose `source` records hold only `confirmed_against_production` loads, and a file whose `source` records hold every provenance field the version-1 format defines loads unchanged.
- [ ] `sqllens validate` exits 2 and `sqllens serve` refuses to start, each with a message naming the cause, for a rule-set file that holds a `row_rule` (the message saying to remove the whole rule set, never only its row rules), for a non-MySQL `database.url`, and for a `binding.database` that differs from the database named in `database.url`, even when it equals `[database] name`.
- [ ] For a rule-set file with unconfirmed sets, `sqllens validate` exits 0 and prints one `Warning:` line naming each unconfirmed set, and `sqllens serve` starts and logs one warning naming each unconfirmed set.
- [ ] With a listed table or listed column missing from the connected MySQL database, a listed name whose letter case differs from the database's, or a listed table that is a view, `sqllens serve` (preflight on) refuses to start and `sqllens validate --check-db` exits 2, each naming the mismatched table or column.
- [ ] With `--no-preflight` and a listed column missing from the database, every rule-set request that passes the five request classes and the conversation-owner check is refused with `isError` before the agent runs, with text saying the rule-set file could not be confirmed against the database and naming no table or column. The server log names the missing column, and once the column exists the next such request is served. A request that also fails one of the five request classes is refused as that class.
- [ ] Each of exactly these five request classes is refused with `isError: true` before the agent runs, with text naming the class and no `_meta` value: rule-set key missing or empty; rule-set name not a string or whole number or naming no set; account key missing or its decimal text not in `binding.account_ids`; user key missing or not a positive whole number; the named set unconfirmed.
- [ ] A rule-set name sent as the number `2` or the string `"2"` selects set `"2"`, while `"02"`, `2.0`, `true`, `null`, `[2]` and `{}` are refused as naming no set. A user ID sent as `7`, `"7"` or `"007"` is accepted as 7, while `0`, `-1`, `"7a"`, `true` and `7.0` are refused as an invalid user ID.
- [ ] A request whose `_meta` has more than 64 keys is refused as rule-set key missing.
- [ ] Under the example set, each of these runs and returns rows: `SELECT c.name, o.total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id`; `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders ORDER BY n`; `SELECT c.name AS nm FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY nm`; `SELECT name FROM customers UNION SELECT name FROM customers ORDER BY name`; `WITH t AS (SELECT c.name AS nm FROM customers c) SELECT t.nm FROM t`; `SELECT d.n FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders o) d`; `SELECT name, total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id`; `SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)`; `SELECT name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE customer_id = c.id)`; `SELECT o.customer_id AS cust, SUM(o.total) AS revenue FROM orders o GROUP BY cust HAVING revenue > 100`; and `SELECT NAME FROM customers`. `SELECT name FROM CUSTOMERS` is refused.
- [ ] Under the example set, a statement that reads `customers.email`, `orders.discount` or the predicate column `customers.rep_id` fails with MySQL's unknown-column error (1054) and returns no value of that column, exactly as `customers.nosuch` does. At minimum these placements of `customers.email` fail this way: the select list, `WHERE`, `JOIN … ON`, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING MAX(customers.email) > ''`, an `ORDER BY` expression, a window `ORDER BY`, a function argument, `customers JOIN orders USING (email)`, a correlated reference from an `EXISTS` subquery, and `SELECT (SELECT x FROM (SELECT email AS x) d) FROM customers`. A statement that reads `salaries` is refused before execution.

With `database.refuse_whole_row_selects = false`, `SELECT * FROM customers` and `SELECT c.* FROM customers c` return only `id` and `name`.
